name: Marigold

schedule.notes: Germinates fast in warm soil — direct-sowing usually catches up to transplants.
Deadhead spent blooms or pinch to keep flowering until frost.

harvest.cues: Flowers fully open, bright yellow to deep orange or red. Snip with shears just above a leaf node.
harvest.storageNotes: Cut flowers last about a week in water — strip lower leaves, they smell strong in vases. Petals dry for confetti.

varieties.name: French Petite (Tagetes patula)
varieties.notes: Compact 8 to 12 in bushes, ideal for bed edges. The classic companion-plant marigold.

varieties.name: African Crackerjack (Tagetes erecta)
varieties.notes: Big pompom heads on 2 to 3 ft plants. Cut-flower staple, Day of the Dead variety.

varieties.name: Lemon Gem (Tagetes tenuifolia)
varieties.notes: Tiny edible flowers, citrus-tarragon scent. Lacy foliage, neat 8 in mounds.

notes: Famous as a vegetable-garden companion — French marigolds release a compound from their roots that suppresses root-knot nematodes (effect builds over the season). Easy from direct seed once soil is warm; deadhead religiously for continuous bloom. Self-seeds in mild winters.
